selection_reason: APW-03 completed_verified in PR #419. The owner-approved interleave selects APW-04 immediately before APM-02.
objective: Define the Personal Workspace and No-Campaign Home so a subscribed/authorized user with zero Campaign memberships still has a useful governed Multiversal environment for owned Characters, creative work, references, practice/sandbox preparation, notifications and account resources while Personal and Campaign contexts remain explicitly separated and no Personal route implies GM/Player/Campaign authority.
completion_gate: A subscribed user with zero Campaign memberships has a useful governed Personal workspace and can move between Personal and Campaign contexts without authority bleed.
required_design_questions: What belongs in Personal Home versus a Campaign Home/Session/Creator Project?
Which resources can be truly Personal-owned and which may only be referenced from Campaign or published/canonical sources?
How are Characters outside Campaigns represented and later proposed/added to Campaigns without ownership/authority confusion?
What practice/sandbox operations are safe in Personal context and how are their outputs kept non-Campaign/noncanonical?
How do CSW Creative Library/Story Bible projects appear in Personal Home?
How are notifications, recent work, drafts, pending invitations and account/entitlement information projected without revealing inaccessible Campaign content?
How does context switching reauthorize navigation, search, caches, recent-item links and AI context?
What happens when a user has zero Campaigns, leaves their last Campaign or loses access?
How are Personal exports/imports/backups/recovery separated from Campaign-private data?
How does APW-04 hand off to APM-02 Cozy Solo without granting Campaign or automation authority?
nonauthorization: Personal route as global GM/Player authority
copying Campaign-private truth into Personal ownership
next_action: Execute APW-04 as a bounded design/governance tranche defining Personal Home resources, context switching/reauthorization, zero-Campaign usability, Character/creative/sandbox boundaries, notifications/recent work and privacy/recovery behavior.
